newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest dealers apply protection on soybeans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest dealers apply protection on soybeans.

text.p: U.S. Midwest grain dealers applied cash price protection of five cents per bushel on soybeans and isolated two cents protection on corn in reaction to Wednesday's bearishly-construed USDA crop reports, grain dealers said.

USDA estimated the U.S. corn crop at 8.804 billion bushels and the soybean crop at 2.270 billion. The soybean estimate exceeded the average trade estimate. The corn estimate was in line with trade estimates, but USDA increased its 1996/97 corn ending stocks estimate to 668 million bushels from its August estimate of 523 million.
CBOT grain analysts said they expect corn futures to open two to four cents per bushel lower and soybean futures five to 10 cents lower in reaction to the USDA reports.
